full_judgment:
3. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that opposite party Nos. 1-3 filed Title Suit No. 99 of 2003 against the present petitioners and 2 Others in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chandpur for specific performance of contact and the said suit was dismissed ex-parte vide judgment and decree dated 17-1-2004 against which the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 82 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Chandpur which was heard by the learned 1st Joint District Judge, Chandpur and after hearing, vide judgment and decree dated 6-7-2010 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. 

 4. Thereafter, the opposite parties filed Title Execution Case being No. 5 of 2010 before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chandpur Sadar, Chandpur. In said case the decree- holders filed application for correction of the schedule of the plaint, decree as well as application for execution which was heard by the learned Assistant Judge and after hearing, vide order dated 20-3-2012 rejected same against which they preferred Civil Revision No. 49 of 2012 before the learned District Judge, Chandpur and the learned District Judge, after hearing, vide judgment dated 22-8-2013 allowed the revision and set-aside the order of the execution Court against which this revisional application has been preferred by two of the defendants of the original suit. 

 6. Mr. AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that by suppressing summons of the suit the opposite parties got a decree from the appellate Court and execution case also proceeded with behind the knowledge of the present petitioners. 

 7. Learned Advocate further submits that the Execution Court has no jurisdiction to entertain any amendment petition for amendment of the plaint and decree and accordingly, the learned Assistant Judge rightly rejected the application filed by opposite parties but the appellate Court without considering the legal aspect and facts and circumstances of the case most illegally and arbitrarily set-aside the order of the Execution Court and allowed amendment of the plaint, decree and application for petition of execution case. 

 8. Learned Advocate further submits that in the meantime, the present petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 60 of 2014 challenging the said ex-parte decree passed in Title Appeal No. 82 of 2014 as well as the sale deed which has been executed and registered through the process of the Court before the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Chandpur and the said suit is now pending for disposal. 

 9. Mr. Md. Salauddin Talukder, learned Advocate appearing for opposite party Nos. 1-3 opposes the Rule and submits that since there was clerical mistake in the plaint, decree of the trial Court as well as in the application for execution and such type of clerical mistake could be amended by the Execution Court, the revisional Court committed no illegality in allowing the amendment by setting aside the order passed by the Execution Court. 

 11. I have heard the learned Advocate of both the parties and perused the revisional application, the impugned judgment and other relevant papers which are available on record. It is an admitted position that opposite party Nos. 1-3 filed suit for specific performance contract which was dismissed ex-parte and thereafter, they obtained decree from the appellate Court ex-pate. It is also admitted that after passing of the impugned judgment by the revisional Court the execution case has been proceeded with and the Executing Court executed the decree by executing and registering the sale deed in favour of opposite party Nos. 1-3, It is also admitted that challenging the judgment and decree passed by the appellant Court in Title Appeal No. 82 of 2014 and the sale deed which has been executed registered on 28-11-2013, the present petitioners filed Title Suit No. 60 of 2014 and in the meantime, PW 1 has been examined by the trial Court. 

 12. It is settle principle that executing Court has no jurisdiction to amend the plaint or decree and, as such, the executing Court rightly rejected the application for amendment It also appears that revisional Court vide impugned order set-aside the order of the Execution Court with some observations, but did not allow the prayer for amendment and directed the Executing Court to take necessary steps in the light of observation made in the judgment which was unwarranted and uncalled for. Since, after passing of the impugned order, the sale deed has executed and registered and the petitioners, in the meantime, have filed Title Suit No. 60 of 2014 against the opposite parties challenging the ex-parte decree passed in Title Appeal No. 82 of 2004 as well as the sale deed, I am of the view that the petitioners could get properly remedy in the said suit.
